scalars.scalar_value: Experience with primary cell engineering, including B cells or other immune cells, and viral vector production (such as lentivirus or AAV).

items.item_text: Must be able to work various hours and locations based on business needs.
Employment is subject to a criminal background check.
Employment is subject to pre-employment physical for those who work in clinical settings and/or with patients.
Performs other duties as assigned.
Complies with all policies and standards.
Complies with the University of California, San Diego Health (UCSDH) Principles of Community.

This position description is not intended to be a complete list of all responsibilities, duties or skills required for the job and is subject to review and change at any time, with or without notice, in accordance with the needs of the organization.
Experience with primary cell engineering, including B cells or other immune cells, and viral vector production (such as lentivirus or AAV).
Experience with spectral flow cytometry and multi-parameter panel design.
Hands-on mouse experience, including live procedures, colony management and tissue harvest.
Experience with human subjects research, including specimen collection and IRB documentation. Background in vaccine research, HIV/infectious disease, or gene therapy.
Demonstrated experience contributing to peer-reviewed publications or conference presentations.
Demonstrated programming experience (e.g., Python) for data analysis.

The Department of Medicine (DOM) is the largest department within the UCSD School of Medicine and is responsible for fulfilling the teaching, research and clinical missions of the University of California, San Diego School of Medicine. The department employs approximately 500 salaried faculty, 168 academic appointees, 331 residents, fellows and postdocs and 480 staff personnel.

Under the general supervision, the Laboratory Manager manages day-to-day operations of a research laboratory and independently carries out complex, multidisciplinary research projects. The lab focuses on B cell gene therapy design and HIV vaccine and functional cure research. They will keep the laboratory running safely, compliantly, and productively. The Laboratory Manager also oversees, directs and trains laboratory staff and produces data that supports publications and grant-funded research. The position works with considerable independence and exercises judgment in designing experiments, troubleshooting, and prioritizing work. Other duties assigned as needed.

Advanced theoretical and practical knowledge of molecular biology, cell biology and immunology principles and laboratory techniques as typically attained through a Bachelor’s degree, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Demonstrated ability to work independently, manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
Demonstrated ability to analyze and organize scientific data and present results clearly, in writing and verbally.
Demonstrated ability to train and mentor others and to work collaboratively with investigators, staff and core facilities.
Strong organizational skills, including inventory and records management.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and data analysis tools.
Advanced skill in experimental design, troubleshooting and optimizing complex protocols.
Advanced skill in DNA/RNA workflows, protein purification, and assays such as ELISA, qPCR and SPR.
